71.prompt:
This is a restoration job, not an illustration job. The attachment is a 2012 game map: an original hand-painted landscape with game markings drawn on top of it. Give me back the same painting with every game marking removed, and sharper. Do not move or redraw anything else.

Remove completely, and paint in what lies underneath so it matches the painting around it:
- the pale yellow-white road lines and ribbons that join the places, and their joints;
- every street name and every word, including "To: ..." labels;
- the small grey sign and house icons along the roads;
- the round "GO" buttons and the small round blue-and-red station badge.
Keep, because they are part of the painting, not markings: the small wooden boards and signposts that stand at some places (parks, preserves, habitats), huts, fences, bridges, ladders and every other painted object, but only the ones you can see in the attachment: never add a board, fence, hut or ladder where the attachment shows a name, an icon or plain ground. Only the markings listed above go.

Where a marking covered something, continue the grass, rock, sand, water, trees or cliffs that surround it, in the same style. Do not add anything new where a marking was: no new trees, rocks, buildings or paths.

The attachment is already the exact size and shape I want back (16:9). The painting fills the middle; the two flat bands at the left and right edges are padding: leave them flat, the same colour, and do not extend the painting into them. Do not stretch, scale, crop, shift or re-frame anything.

Everything that is part of the painting must come back at exactly the same position, size, angle and shape, so that the result laid over the attachment matches line for line: every coastline, cliff edge, river, field edge, tree, bush, rock, cloud, building and shadow. Keep the colours, the lighting and the overall brightness exactly as they are; do not make it more saturated, darker or more contrasty.

Make it crisper than a plain enlargement: remove the JPEG blocks and blur, make the existing edges crisp, and bring out the brushwork and texture already there. If you are unsure whether something is part of the painting or a marking, keep it.

No text of your own, no lines, no border, no frame, no watermark.

Same picture again. Do not add anything that is not in the attachment: no new wooden boards, signposts, fences, huts or ladders. Where a grey icon, a street name or a road ran, continue the ground, trees or rock around it. Keep only the objects you can see in the attachment, and keep the small garden plot with its green rows at the left end of the middle (Tallus Gardens) as it is there.
